country: Democratic Republic of the Congo (Zaïre in 1984)
census: Recensement scientifique de la population, juillet 1984
the_only_census: No census has been taken since. The second (RGPH-2) was in its preparatory phase in September 2026, with census mapping under way in Kinshasa and no published date for enumeration.

source.title: Zaïre. Recensement scientifique de la population, juillet 1984. Totaux définitifs
source.publisher: République du Zaïre, Ministère du Plan et Aménagement du Territoire, Institut National de la Statistique

tables.T-01: Répartition de la population résidante du Zaïre par Région, printed page 12
tables.T-02: Répartition de la population résidante du Zaïre par Région et Sous-Région, printed pages 13 to 16

Zongo, Bukavu and Kananga rows unreadable as text

units: counts.csv: the country, 9 regions, and their 44 cities (villes) and sub-regions (sous-régions), as printed. A ville is a unit of the same level as a sous-région: a region's total is the sum of both. units.csv places each of the 44 in one of today's 26 provinces; provinces-2015.csv sums the counts to them. Both are written by scripts/cod_provinces.py.

reviewed.found: First transcription. RGPH-2 in its preparatory phase, no enumeration date.

provinces_2015.label: Summed to today's 26 provinces (2015)
provinces_2015.what: The 1984 counts summed to the 26 provinces of 2015, so they can be matched to a map of today's provinces. Derived, not printed: the counts are still those of July 1984.

law.title: Loi organique n° 15/006 du 25 mars 2015 portant fixation des limites des provinces et celles de la ville de Kinshasa
law.published: Journal officiel de la République Démocratique du Congo, numéro spécial, 28 mars 2015
law.used_for: the 26 provinces' names (article 2) and each province's chef-lieu (articles 4 onwards)

boundaries.what: geoBoundaries gbOpen COD ADM1 and ADM2 at commit 9469f09, as held in digital-twin-ph/boundaries
boundaries.used_for: each province's spelling and ID, and the province each 1984 city lies in (the ADM2 unit's point inside an ADM1 polygon); each law chef-lieu was checked to lie in the province it heads

provinces_2015.how: A sub-region goes to the province of the same name (Haut-Shaba to Haut-Katanga, Shaba having been renamed Katanga in 1997; Kabinda to Lomami, whose chef-lieu it is; Lulua to Kasaï Central, around Kananga; Tshilenge to Kasaï Oriental, around Mbuji-Mayi). A city goes to the province it lies in. Kinshasa's four sub-regions and the whole of Bas-Zaïre go to Kinshasa and Kongo Central.
does_not_establish: That each 1984 sub-region's limits are the 2015 province's. The law draws limits along rivers and lines, not by former units, and any territory moved between units since 1984 moves its people with it here only if the move followed unit lines.

Where the land of the Plateaux district (Bolobo, Kwamouth, Mushie, Yumbi: Mai-Ndombe province today) was counted in 1984. Bandundu region printed three sub-regions; if any of it was then in Kwilu, Kwilu here is too high and Mai-Ndombe too low by those people.
That the law and geoBoundaries agree beyond the chefs-lieux: geoBoundaries' lines are OpenStreetMap's, not the law's.
